study.question: Does supplied direction in the local and coarse linear history summaries carry useful information beyond each summary vector up to sign, or did two-view sign averaging lose quality through its optimization/readout constraints?
study.hypothesis: The larger loss for coarse than local sign averaging may reflect useful signed coarse direction, but per-view BCE and joint two-view normalization are competing explanations. A deterministic maximum-coordinate orientation removes only the global sign of each selected vector with the original single-view architecture and loss. If the unoriented vectors recover signed-control click AUC, sign-averaging failure did not establish directional necessity; persistent losses under the two replacement families provide conditional, still preliminary evidence for useful orientation. This is a local hypothesis, not a novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text lines264-283 and317-335 describes target-conditioned unnormalized pooling and Dice. Retain inherited adaptation, but test sign quotient of existing local/coarse moments in joint context/history model. The paper LSTM null does not transfer to this task.

Authorized section2.3 describes joint interaction families and LONGER group compression; benchmark descriptions are not an original-method audit. No new Transformer, token hub or sparse filter is introduced. Exact priority of sign canonicalization is unverified.

Previously average shared-network probabilities for +m and -m with per-view BCE and2B Dice population. Now canonicalize m once before all learned consumers, retain the original single-view loss andB population, and compare a fresh matched signed bridge. Historical results are contextual, not a matched estimate of only readout location.

study.proposed_difference: Four-cell factorial over canonicalize_local and canonicalize_coarse. For each selected summary vector m, use sign of its first maximum-absolute coordinate to choose between m and -m; pivot selection detached in FP32, multiplication preserves original dtype. No trainable parameters, extra views, loss override, or changes to event eligibility. Unselected bridge returns original tensors exactly while still computing both alternatives.
predictions: signed_bridge should reproduce g0-r0052-block_nonlinear_transfer click AUC0.6685268680116033 within host numeric tolerance, with exactly32192421 parameters and399205 dense parameters; native equality is a required host check, not an observed result.

If supplied coarse direction is predictive beyond its axis, coarse_axis loses validation click AUC to signed_bridge; local_axis is predicted to lose less, based on r0066. Direction estimates are preliminary at one seed.

If two-view optimization/readout explains most of r0066 loss, the canonical cells recover much of its gap without extra views. Restoration would favor further direct invariant replacements rather than declaring history direction necessary.

joint_axis will identify interaction via (A_joint-A_local)-(A_coarse-A_bridge), without treating AUC as additive probability. It removes independent vector signs, unlike simultaneous two-view sign averaging which retains relative sign.
Sign-quotient cells satisfy g(m)=g(-m), g(g(m))=g(m), and preserve norm and outer product at fixed values; full event-order invariance is not predicted.
Single-view cost should be near the inherited approximately381s unit rather than the approximately598-617s two-view units; actual time, memory and latency must be measured.
falsifiers: Any changed eligibility, invalid-slot influence, extra input, target action use, native parity/gradient failure or altered learned capacity invalidates the intended contrast.
Reproducible canonical performance equal/better than signed_bridge falsifies the claim that selected moment direction is needed in this replacement setting.
Persistent losses do not falsify all invariant modeling; pivot-boundary instability, changed normalization or limited optimization may explain them.
If signed_bridge fails incumbent parity, repair the common implementation before interpreting canonical effects.
If local_axis loses more than coarse_axis in repeated matched runs, the predicted coarse-dominant effect is falsified.
If canonicalization overhead erases saved compute versus previous two-view treatments, reject the efficiency prediction even if quality recovers.
alternative_explanations: Argmax orientation is piecewise smooth and discontinuous when the largest absolute coordinate changes; learned embedding basis and optimizer can affect stability.
Canonicalization changes the distribution seen by adapters and native Dice even at matched parameter count.
Other channels retain order; representation-level sign invariance does not imply event reversal or permutation invariance.
One frozen training seed gives preliminary evidence and repeated incumbent bridges are not independent seeds.
Historical canonical sort/path losses can arise from grouping and coefficient alignment; they do not alone isolate direction.
Support gates, quadratic moments and block compression still reveal aspects of supplied order; a good canonical result cannot establish content-only sufficiency.
Validation has been queried repeatedly across many designs; small gains may reflect adaptive selection and need paired repetitions followed by a frozen held-out suite.
